provenance: OC-026: SPARC Central Solenoid Model Coil (CSMC) screening parity from the published record only - CFS press release 2024-11-18 (50 kA, 5.7 T, 20 K, ~4 T/s, tested Aug-Oct 2024 at MIT PSFC); Baldini/Marchevsky ASC 2024 slides (4 nested layers x 10 turns, 1.2 m inner diameter, stored energy 3.728 MJ); Sanabria et al., SUST 37 (2024) 115010 (PIT-VIPER cable: 4 partitioned Cu petals each holding a REBCO tape stack, 23-25 mm cable OD class); IAEA FEC 2025 CFS overview (4-layer, 10-turn, first layer tested to 43.3 kA). Modeled: circular layer-wound solenoid, 4 radial layers x 10 axial cable turns = 40 cable turns at 0.648 m path radius (1.2 m ID + half the 96 mm radial build at 24 mm pitch). NOT PUBLISHED and inferred: tapes per petal stack (swept as strands_parallel over the plausible 100-180 tapes-per-cable range, i.e. 25-45 per petal - the case is a conditional certificate across the uncertain parameter, not a fitted answer); exact cable pitch (24 mm nominal from the 23-25 mm published OD range); axial height (~0.24 m from 10 turns x pitch). The published 5.7 T figure is not labeled bore-center or peak-on-conductor in the public record; the run result resolves the ambiguity - the modeled winding needs 52.4 kA for a declared 2.0 T bore-center target (~5% from the published 50 kA operating current), while the modeled peak sampled field at that operating point is ~4.9 T, consistent with 5.7 T being a peak-on-conductor-class figure within the inferred-geometry band. The requirement is declared at bore center. Material screening uses robinson-superpower-ap-v3-modelext (measured + declared model extension) - the CSMC tape suppliers are not public; the case certifies the winding, not a vendor choice. Operating point declared at 25 K (the built coil runs 20 K). Same declared limits/costs as oc-025; prices are synthetic.
